/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 01 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3157 (-29)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5221 (-115)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2360 (45)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1650 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 885 (4)
CAPESIZE
The market had a somewhat mixed start to the week, following yesterday’s UK holiday, with no index published. The Pacific softened modestly, while the Atlantic showed some improvement, although activity remained relatively subdued overall. The BCI 182 5TC fell by $1,049 to $47,350, with the C5 index dropping 0.840 to $15.340. Pacific sentiment was a touch softer, despite three C5 miners being in the market. Offers began the day in the upper $15s, with one miner initially heard bidding in the high $14s before levels gradually converged. Reports towards the close indicated $15.25 paid by one miner, while a second was said to have fixed at $15.40. This compared with $15.50 reportedly paid a couple of times yesterday. The Atlantic was more positive, albeit with a sluggish start to the week. C3 edged up 0.136 to $38.50, with $38.50 reported paid for 26 September onwards, following $38.50 fixed on C3 for 3/5 October yesterday. Bids for index dates were heard around $37.75-$38.00 against offers in the mid-$38s to $39. Brokers are also reporting an increase in ballasters for end-September dates, adding some potential pressure to the Atlantic tonnage position.
PANAMAX
The positive sentiment seen last week continued, with both basins posting rate increases. The P5TC rose by $403 to close at $21,237. Trans-Atlantic and fronthaul routes were reported by some market sources to have a relatively wide bid-offer spread as the market exhibited a typical Monday feel following the UK public holiday, as both Charterers and Owners assessed market conditions, their respective positions and corresponding rate expectations. The North Atlantic was described as relatively well supplied with tonnage, however some market participants noted that the situation may not be as straightforward as it appears, as several vessels currently being reported as available may already have employment pencilled in behind them. Market participants also highlighted continued demand for mid-to-late September cargoes, which could provide further support to current rate levels. The Antiparos (81,640 2013) fixed basis passing Falmouth for a trans-Atlantic round with minerals at $21,250. In the Pacific, market fundamentals were described as firm, with the stronger sentiment continuing to underpin rates. The P6 route was reported to be active today, showing improved signs of demand and providing further employment opportunities for tonnage open in the Far East. Australian coal demand was also highlighted as robust, particularly for prompt-loading dates, which provided additional support to the market.
SUPRAMAX
The start of a new week for those of us in the UK, and still the market lacks any clear direction, with the 11TC average up $39 to $20,858. The Baoshan Glory (56,686 2012) Karachi 15 September was said to have fixed for 12 months at $16,900, but no further details came to light.

Atlantic
Oldendorff were rumoured to have taken a 63,000-dwt delivery Corpus Christi for a trip East Mediterranean with petcoke at $33,000, a 61,000-dwt open Baltimore was said to have fixed a trip to Tampa with aggregates at $25,000 with Pangaea and a Ultramax fixed delivery Baie Commeau for a trip Lagos intention grains at $29,500 with ABCML.

Asia
The Sapphire Eternity (63,610 2025) prompt Lianyungang fixed a NoPac round voyage at around $21,000 and Allianz booked the Baranee Naree (56,441 2012) Campha 3-7 September for a trip Bangladesh with clinker in the low $20,000’s. The Tomini Unity (63,590 2017) Rizhao 1-5 September was rumoured fixed for a trip US Gulf in the $13,000’s by Panocean and the Cl Shaoyang (64,758 2024) prompt Karachi went on subjects delivery Port Elizabeth trip China with WBC at $25,000 plus $250,000 ballast bonus.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market opened the week on a quiet note following the long weekend, with sentiment remaining largely positional across most regions. The BHSI edged up by 4 points to 885, while the 7TC average gained $78 to close at $15,933. Across the Continent and Mediterranean the market started slowly, with fundamentals broadly unchanged. The South Atlantic saw pockets of activity, with fundamentals remaining firm and rates heard above last-done levels. The US Gulf continued to move at a subdued pace, with very limited fixing activity and flat sentiment prevailing. On the Pacific side, despite an increase in open tonnage, overall levels remained healthy. Period levels also appeared to be holding firm, with the TS Index (38,854 2018) open Fangcheng reported fixed for 5 to 7 months at $17,500 by Panocean, although further details were not disclosed.

Atlantic
The Ultra Osorno (37,981 2018) was reported fixed from Recalada to West Coast South America in the high $20,000s. Meanwhile, the Hydra Dawn (34,274 2013) fixed from Recalada to the North of Fortaleza range with grains at $19,000 by Fednav, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
A 42,000-dwt vessel open in the Far East was reported fixed for two laden legs with redelivery in the Singapore–Japan range at close to $20,000. Separately, a 28,000-dwt vessel open in South Africa was fixed for a trip via Saldanha Bay to ARAG in the $12,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
China’s Manufacturing PMI

China’s manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose 0.6 points from the prior month to 49.8 in August, although still stood below the 50-mark separating expansion from contraction, marking a second consecutive month of contraction, National Bureau of Statistics show.

CISA Daily Crude Steel Production

In the period 11-20 August, daily crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills eased 0.4% from the preceding ten days to 2.0 Mt/day and down 7.1% on the year, industry association data show.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape curve saw a strong late-session rally after a softer start. September was the main focus, trading between 44,750–46,750, with early activity around 45,000–45,750 before pushing sharply higher through the afternoon. October traded between 45,600–47,150, also strengthening into the close. The Sep v Oct spread widened and strengthen to -250 while the Oct v Q4 traded sideways at 2000 and Nov v Dec 2500. PACIFIC: The market started the week quietly, with overall sentiment relatively subdued. Most regions showed limited activity and flat performance. In SEA, Indo coal remained quiet. Offers for Indo/China remained modest, with SMX levels from Singapore offering around 16k, showing no significant upward movement. The gap between chtrs bid and owners offer still huge. The Indo/India sector saw some interest but was not particularly active either. Overall, the SEA coal market felt flat with limited price exchange. Aussie cargoes were also not very active this week. Cargo volumes remained limited, and charterers were not aggressive in their calculations. Rates for Auseie iron ore and grain stayed at moderate levels, while West Australian salt and grain saw steady but limited demand. The north general cargo market was relatively quiet and flat this week. Backhaul cargoes just regularly came out and market activity was moderate. An eco UMX open in CJK for general cargo to WAfrica was still around 20-21k, while Med directions saw similar levels without significant changes. The Nopac market showed relatively decent numbers this week, but fresh cargoes were not abundant. Charterers' ideas for Nopac grain to Chittagong were around 21500, with some fixtures heard at similar levels. Although rates remained respectable, the lack of significant new cargo volumes kept the market from gaining strong upward momentum. ECI remained weak, with local iron ore exports continuing to perform poorly. Many owners preferred to ballast to SEA still rather than fix at such low levels. WCI was similarly weak, the market lacked strong driving factors, and conditions remained generally poor. South Africa stood out as the most active region this week, with vessel-chasing sentiment evident. An eco UMX based in safrica could achieve 25k+250k APS for SAfrica cargo back to the Fareast, reflecting a firm market with healthy cargo demand. In summary, most regions remained flat with limited activity this week, except for South Africa, which continued to show strength with vessels being chased and rates reaching higher levels. We look forward to seeing how the market performs going forward.
